comment: Cross-language golden vectors for the per-invite team name and the classroom50/invite/v1 record stored in its description. Both writers of this contract must produce these bytes for these inputs: the web (inviteTeamName / marshalInviteDescription in web/src/util/inviteTeam.ts, asserted by web/src/util/inviteTeam.test.ts) and the teacher CLI (InviteTeamName / MarshalInviteDescription in cli/gh-teacher/internal/configrepo/invite_team.go, asserted by invite_team_test.go). `slug` is `invite-` + the first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 over `<classroom>\u0000<normalized email>`; normalization is trim + lowercase, applied before BOTH the hash and the stored `email` so a roster row can always relocate its team. `record` is the EXACT description bytes — compact JSON in schema/email/classroom order with Go json.Marshal's HTML and U+2028/U+2029 escaping — because a reconcile compares descriptions for string equality, so a byte difference would make the two writers overwrite each other forever. Update both writers in lockstep; regenerating a vector means the wire contract changed and every already-created invite team becomes unlocatable.

cases.why: the canonical invite: an already-normalized email and a simple classroom
mixed case and surrounding whitespace normalize FIRST, so this is the same team and record as the canonical case
the same email in a second classroom hashes to a distinct team, so one org can invite it twice
boundary pair A: without the \u0000 separator ("ab","c@x") and ("a","bc@x") would hash the same bytes
boundary pair B: must not equal pair A's slug
a hyphenated classroom short-name and a plus-tagged address
Go json.Marshal HTML-escapes <, >, and & — the record bytes carry \u003c/\u003e/\u0026, never the raw chars
Go json.Marshal escapes the U+2028/U+2029 line and paragraph separators too

the WHOLE C0 range plus DEL, where the two encoders AGREE code point for code point: U+0008/U+0009/U+000A/U+000C/U+000D take the same short \b/\t/\n/\f/\r JSON.stringify emits (never \u0008/\u000c), every other C0 control takes the same lowercase \u00xx, and DEL is left raw by both — so the web's Go-parity escaper must touch none of them. Exhaustive on purpose: the escaper's claim is that <, >, & and U+2028/U+2029 are the ONLY divergences, and a range checked in part is a claim pinned in part. Synthetic input: it pins the escaping contract, not a realistic classroom name.
